sources.entry: BannerHither - Menu bar app that moves macOS notification banners to the display you are looking at: the screen under the mouse pointer, the screen of the active window, or a fixed display.

summary.one_liner: BannerHither is a macOS menu bar app that moves system notification banners to whichever display you are using, instead of the primary display where macOS always draws them.
summary.what_it_does: BannerHither watches NotificationCenter through the public Accessibility API and, when a banner appears, sets the banner window's position so it lands on a chosen display. The target can be the screen under the mouse pointer, the screen of the active window (with the mouse screen as fallback), or one fixed display; a "System default" option leaves macOS behaviour alone. It runs as a menu bar item with no Dock icon, with Start/Stop, Launch at Login, a test notification with a 3-second delay, and a Copy Diagnostics item. The README says it moves the whole NotificationCenter window rather than reading notification contents, and it can optionally check for updates once a day. Advanced settings (poll interval, resizing the window to the target display, an alternative update feed) are set through UserDefaults since they have no menu item.
use_cases: show macOS notifications on my external monitor
move notification banners to the screen I'm working on
keep banners off the primary display
pin notifications to one fixed display
debug notification window position on macOS
how_to_run: Or download BannerHither-<version>.dmg from the Releases page and drag BannerHither.app to Applications
notable: Moves the entire NotificationCenter window via AXPosition, so clicks, swipes and close buttons keep working
Acts only on banner-appear and repositioning transitions, so banners don't follow the mouse once shown
Universal binary with UI in English, Korean, Japanese, Simplified Chinese, German, French and Spanish
Needs only the Accessibility permission; no notification contents are read
Optional daily update check; the app does not self-install updates
caveats: Relies on undocumented NotificationCenter behaviour that Apple may change in any macOS update
Only macOS 26.6 is verified; macOS 14.0 to 15.x is stated to build and should work but is untested
Not tested with 'Displays have separate Spaces' off, Stage Manager, or on the lock screen; mirrored displays are not separate targets
keywords: send notifications to my second display
